issues.legal_issue: A will’s earlier disposition of property after a life interest remains effective under a later adoption contingency when the will, read as a whole, shows that the contingency provisions modify only specified gifts and do not revoke that disposition.
material_facts: The will gave a daughter a life interest in a village and provided that after her death the property would pass to another daughter and her children, subject to a payment to the life tenant’s daughter.

A later paragraph provided that the village would be enjoyed by the life tenant as stated in the earlier paragraph, but did not repeat the earlier paragraph’s disposition of the property after the life interest.
The will addressed alternative adoption contingencies and made specific changes to certain gifts while leaving the earlier disposition of the village unaltered.
The widow adopted a son of the testator’s nephew, and after the life tenant died, the adopted son claimed the village on the basis that the will left the remainder undisposed of.
issues.conclusion: The earlier paragraph applied despite the adoption of a nephew’s son. The village passed to the designated daughter after the life tenant’s death, subject to the stated payment, and the claim that it passed to the adopted son as heir was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The primary aim in construing a will is to ascertain the testator’s intention from the language of the document read as a whole. Surrounding circumstances and the testator’s family position may assist in interpreting the language, but a court may not add to the dispositions once the will is construed. A presumption against intestacy may assist only where there is undoubted ambiguity; it cannot displace the plain meaning of words. The Court applied the principles stated in Venkatanarasimha v. Parthasarathy (41 I.A. 51) and Re Edward; Jones v. Jones ([1906] 1 Ch. 570).

rule.if: will_construction_dispute and integrated_contingency_scheme and earlier_clause_disposes_remainder and later_clause_repeats_only_life_interest and earlier_disposition_is_not_modified

predicates.will_construction_dispute: The dispute concerns the meaning and effect of dispositions in a will.
predicates.integrated_contingency_scheme: The will addresses alternative future contingencies and makes specified modifications to its dispositions for those contingencies.
predicates.earlier_clause_disposes_remainder: An earlier clause provides who takes property after a life tenant’s interest ends.
predicates.later_clause_repeats_only_life_interest: A later clause refers to the life tenant’s enjoyment of the property without restating who takes after that interest ends.
predicates.earlier_disposition_is_not_modified: The will does not otherwise alter or revoke the earlier clause’s disposition of the property after the life interest.
predicates.earlier_remainder_beneficiary_takes_afte: The person designated by the earlier clause takes the property after the life tenant’s interest ends.

issues.definition: When a will addresses alternative contingencies, an earlier disposition of the remainder governs if a later clause only restates the life interest and does not modify that disposition.
